limitations: offline in-memory microbenchmark, not deployed near-real-time RIC timing
amortized batch microseconds per report, not per-request tail latency
excludes telemetry, transport, serialization, scheduling, and actuation
shared virtualized host load and frequency can affect wall-clock results
Linux RSS/HWM includes process and inputs; incremental memory is observational

protocol.cold_definition: first invocation with model and input already resident
protocol.warm_definition: recorded invocations after first call and unreported warmups

memory.interpretation: Linux whole-process resident memory; inputs and interpreter are included. The high-water increment is observational and allocator reuse can make it understate transient workload demand.
